root_cause.text: The function `__iommu_group_set_domain_internal()` unconditionally rejected all domain attachment requests when any device in the group was recovering (`group->recovery_cnt` nonzero), even for callers that set the `IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED` flag (e.g., teardown/detach paths), causing a WARN_ON in the nofail path and a use-after-free when `pci_dev_reset_iommu_done()` later re-attached the freed domain.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the rejection condition from `if (group->recovery_cnt)` to `if (group->recovery_cnt && !(flags & IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED))`, and adds a `gdev->blocked` check in the device iteration loop to skip devices under recovery. The commit message explicitly states: "Other IOMMU_SET_DOMAIN_MUST_SUCCEED callers ... should not be rejected, as the domain would be freed anyway ... So pci_dev_reset_iommu_done() could trigger a UAF when re-attaching group->domain."

vuln_statements.explanation: Variable declaration in the function that contains the vulnerable recovery_cnt check; part of the teardown path that fails due to the unconditional rejection.
Variable declaration in the same function; used for iterating group devices which are affected by the improper domain change rejection.
Variable used to store results; the function's early return from the recovery_cnt check bypasses proper result assignment, eventually leading to WARN_ON.
Variable for return values; the early -EBUSY return prevents domain detachment and triggers use-after-free.
Lock assertion; the vulnerability lies in the subsequent conditional that may return -EBUSY even when the mutex is held and the caller has MUST_SUCCEED flag.
